english.title: Driver of a vehicle carrying dangerous / pressurised goods fail to carry transport documents re nature / quantity

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2009

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) drove a vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..), on a road, namely **(..SPECIFY THE LOCATION..), and failed to ensure that the goods or equipment, namely **(..SPECIFY THE CHARACTER OF THE GOODS / EQUIPMENT..), carried on that vehicle which were subject to the Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2009, had

(A)_[the appropriate transportation documents]_
(B)_[transportation documents containing the appropriate details]_

relating to

(C)_[the nature of]_
(D)_[the quantity of]_
(E)_[the nature and quantity of]_

that load
english.legislation: Contrary to regulation 5 of the Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2009 and section 33(1)(c) and (3) of the Health and Safety at Work etc Act 1974.

english.notes:
(i) For further guidance see the prosecution guide.
(ii) In the first instance a prohibition notice under section 22 of the Health and Safety at Work Act 1974 should be considered subject to current HSE policy. Failure to comply with that prohibition should result in prosecution. Care should however be taken to obtain evidence to prove that the operator in the interim period had not complied with and therefore discharged the prohibition notice.
(iii) Where there is evidence of multiple offences, blatant disregard of the regulations or there has been previous advice, prosecution should also be considered.
(iv) The information specified in ADR 5.4 was relevant and should form part of the transportation documents.
(v) The word "appropriate" is open to interpretation.
(vi) A prohibition notice is appropriate if the information is so lacking that the inspector is unable to identify what is being carried
(vii) ADR 2009 section 5.4.1. refers.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: A fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
